subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khanna <samira.khanna@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and next steps. Please reply with anything I missed.

Pain points you shared:
- High p95 latency variability on peak traffic (user-facing search and chat flows) impacting conversions.
- Regulatory requirement to isolate PHI workloads and maintain VPC-level network separation.
- Unpredictable cost from bursty peak traffic; need predictable unit economics for budgeting.

Goals:
- Stable p95 latency <= 50ms for standard chat generation (95th percentile under expected traffic profile).
- Dedicated GPU pools with tenant isolation (VPC + encryption at rest) for PHI workload.
- Predictable monthly committed spend with ability to scale to ~24 GPUs in Q3 if adoption grows.

Proposed dedicated-capacity plan (high level):
- Initial reserved capacity: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) allocated to Aurora Health. This maps to 2 nodes of 4 GPUs for redundancy.
- Autoscaling policy: scheduled and reactive scaling to add up to 24 GPUs (burst to shared reserved pool) with warm-standby pre-warmed instances for fast ramp.
- Isolation & compliance: Private deployment with customer VPC peering, KMS integration for key management, audit logs exported to your SIEM.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool, fallback routing to a verified hosted model if capacity is temporarily constrained (graceful degradation).
- Cost model: monthly reserved commit for base 8-GPU capacity + pay-as-you-go for bursts and additional ephemeral units. We'll include options for annual commit discount.

Recommendations we discussed:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts to reduce token cost on chat search paths.
- Start with a 2-week load test with synthetic traffic to validate latency SLOs before full cutover.

Attachments included: Aurora_Dedicated_Proposal_v3.pdf (detailed sizing & pricing), MAP_Aurora_Redwood.xlsx (mutual action plan).

Next steps:
1) I’ll send a pricing & timeline proposal (attached).
2) Technical deep-dive with Rishi to validate model profile and load test plan — proposed window Fri Apr 23 or Mon Apr 26.
3) Procurement review of MSA & SOC2 evidence (I attached a SOC2 summary).

Would you prefer Fri 4/23 10–11am PT or Mon 4/26 9–10am PT for the technical session?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap, this captures our needs well. A couple quick clarifications:
- The 8 A100-equivalent starting point makes sense as a committed baseline. Can you confirm expected p95 latency at that size for our smallest prompt profile (avg 1.2k tokens)?
- For the scaling plan, what's the expected warm-up time to add capacity to reach ~24 GPUs from 8 during a burst?
- On isolation: we need confirmation that logs containing PHI will not be stored in shared indices and that KMS keys can be customer-managed.

Procurement (cc'd) will need the formal quote and MSA redlines. Can you include an approximate monthly commit price and a separate line for burst usage pricing?

Friday 4/23 10am PT works for the technical deep-dive for Rishi and your team.

Thanks,
Samira Khanna

Thanks Samira — great, glad Friday works. Answers below and attached updated proposal with a price band.

Latency estimate (8 GPU baseline):
- Based on your prompt profile (1.2k tokens typical, 1.2k context), we estimate p95 generation latency ~40–60ms using an optimized model variant (quantized profile) on 8 A100-equivalent GPUs with our continuous batching enabled. Exact numbers will be validated during the 2-week load run.

Scaling & warm-up:
- Scheduled scale (pre-warm) adds nodes within ~3–5 minutes if we spin up from warm images; reactive cold start to fully provision additional GPUs can be 12–20 minutes depending on region capacity. We recommend scheduled pre-warm windows for traffic patterns you flagged.

Isolation & logs:
- PHI data: Our Private deployment option supports customer-managed KMS keys and VPC peering. Audit logs containing PHI can be exported directly to your SIEM and stripped from shared indices — SOC controls are documented in the attached SOC2_Type2_Summary.pdf.

Pricing snapshot (attached proposal):
- Monthly reserved (8 GPUs): $68,000/month (includes 24/7 support & 99.9% SLA).
- Burst capacity (to 24 GPUs): billed at $12,000 per GPU-hour for ephemeral usage beyond reserved capacity, with a cap negotiated in the MAP.
- Load test & onboarding credit: one week of free burst capacity for validation.

Attachments included: Aurora_Dedicated_Proposal_v3.pdf (updated with price bands), MAP_Aurora_Redwood.xlsx, SOC2_Type2_Summary.pdf.

I’ve attached a proposed MAP with milestones and a draft MSA link. If procurement can share their standard timeline for PO + legal review, we’ll align our internal onboarding to meet that date.

Proposed tech deep-dive: Fri Apr 23, 10:00–11:00am PT (Calendly link: https://calendly.com/redwood/aurora-tech-deep-dive). Rishi will cover model profiling and load-test design.

Best,
Marissa
